sittings.bodyEn: On Christmas Eve a payment company froze about $120,000 for six months and called the hold a precaution. The account still showed a little over $23,000, and a salesperson was owed about $22,000 on sales the company had never received. He wired that commission anyway, and the balance fell to about $1,000. In a dark theater his pulse sat near 100 beats a minute, about twice a resting rate for someone sitting still. He kept a screenshot of the account because he already knew the moment would matter later. A booked sale becomes money you can use only after it clears.

terms.hook: A sale you can spend only after the payment actually arrives.

sittings.bodyEn: About thirty days earlier he had sold five of six gyms and parked the proceeds with a new partner as seed money for a company called Gym Launch. The plan was to fly to other gyms and fill them with a method he had already used in his own locations. One morning the balance read $300, after a withdrawal of about $45,700 that had gone to the partner. The gyms, the equipment, and the employees were already gone. In that same stretch his mother was in critical care after an accident, and he had wrecked his car in a head-on crash and picked up a DUI. The one cash event still working was a challenge offer that collected the full fee up front, and his salesperson had sold about $120,000 of it in a month.

terms.hook: The new company: fill other people's gyms with a method already proven in his own.
A turnaround fee collected up front, before months of delivery.

sittings.bodyEn: He told the woman who had stayed that he was a sinking ship and that she was free to leave. She said she would stay even if they ended up sleeping under a bridge, and her friends had already quit jobs to help. He warned that the launches could go badly, and she said she trusted him to figure it out. What remained was a grand slam offer and an old business card with a $100,000 limit from the gym years. The day after Christmas they were due to launch six gyms at the same time. Airfare, hotels, cars, gas, and ads came to about $3,300 a day, about $412 an hour, charged to money he did not have.

terms.hook: The offer strong enough to sell when the locations and the cash are already gone.

sittings.bodyEn: He was selling a result he had already produced, a full gym, using the same method. The fee arrived up front, which is what made a credit-card launch possible while the card was billed every morning. A fee that shows up only after a long delivery cycle cannot repay a daily advertising bill. His hand shook when he switched the ads from off to on. Each day the balance moved further below zero: nothing, then less than nothing, then thousands less than nothing. The test was whether strangers would pay during the launches, fast enough to cover that burn.

terms.hook: Payment that arrives before the work, so it can fund the ads that find the next buyer.

sittings.bodyEn: He later pulled the processing records for January 2017. That month collected $100,117. The amount was just enough to cover the $3,300 a day coming off the card. The same decision that felt like it would ruin him had produced a working month. The conversation moved from bankruptcy lawyers to a machine that was actually collecting cash. The offer had to return money inside the month, and this structure did.

terms.hook: The offer has to return cash inside the same period the ads are being charged.

sittings.bodyEn: By the end of that year the company was doing more than $1,500,000 a month. Twelve months later it was about $4,400,000 a month. Twenty-four months after that, sales had crossed $120,000,000, and they had donated $2,000,000 toward opportunity in low-income areas. They also joined the board of a charity led by a lifelong hero of his. A later portfolio of seven companies, across photography, publishing, fitness, consulting, and beauty, was doing about $1,600,000 a week. Those firms included local chains, software, services, online stores, and training.

terms.hook: Several companies in different trades, built after the first offer worked.

sittings.bodyEn: He names three reasons the year turned: a person who stayed, a credit line, and a grand slam offer. Belief and the card made the test possible. Strangers paid because the offer was specific enough to buy during a launch. Willingness without a clear trade only spends the card. The story jumps from a broken Christmas to a large company on purpose. The rest of the book is the how, and he is explicit that offer-making is the skill he can teach.

terms.hook: The repeatable ability to build a trade people will pay for, taught in the chapters after this story.

sittings.bodyEn: He lists a long run of bad decisions and still says this one skill is the thing he learned deeply. A reader who is actually reading is already unusual, because most people buy material and never open it. He also says the later chapters hold the larger pieces. This chapter is the proof that offer skill can change a year. The pricing steps and the value steps come after the story. Treat the year as evidence the skill is learnable, then build the offer on your own business.

terms.hook: This chapter shows the result, and the following chapters show the build.

sittings.bodyEn: The processor held the sales cash, a partner had taken the seed money, and the gyms were gone. A daily advertising bill still had to be paid for six launches at once. Two assets were left when those launches went live. Choose the pair this chapter says was still usable.
sittings.prompt: What was still usable when the launches started?
choices: A proven offer and a business credit line
The frozen processor balance and the gyms he had already sold
A lower monthly price and a new logo
Waiting six months for the held funds to be released
